title: Encoded strings belong to the decoding language
statement: Let $A$ be a type with an encoding $e:A\to\{0,1\}^*$ and a partial decoder $d:\{0,1\}^*\to A$. Suppose decoding an encoded object recovers it, so $d(e(a))=a$ for every $a\in A$, and every successfully decoded string is the encoding of its decoded object. The language consisting of strings on which $d$ is defined contains $e(a)$ for every $a\in A$.
hypotheses_covered: Decoding each encoded object recovers that object
